settings.integrationsInfo: Optional extras. Nothing here is required to play; imports only link games already on your disk.
settings.surfaceDesc: True black is the default. Soft Black lifts the background and panels a touch — easier on the eyes in bright rooms.
settings.coverStatsDesc: Shows playtime and achievement progress on library covers.
settings.hiddenEmptyDesc: No hidden games. Nothing embarrassing tucked away either.
settings.netCacheDesc: Epic: Safely purges temporary download segments and cached chunks.
settings.autoDesktopShortcutDesc: Epic: Automatically create a desktop shortcut when a game is downloaded and installed.

settings.eosNotSupported: This EOS version may not support overlay installation.

settings.startWithWindowsDesc: Opens the launcher automatically when you sign in.

cover.title: Customize Images
cover.portraitDesc: The portrait cover shown in the library grid and lists. Pick a cover you like from SteamGridDB or paste a web link.
cover.heroDesc: The cinematic wide banner used as the background in the home spotlight, detail drawer and shelves.
cover.resetAllTip: Revert both the portrait cover and wide hero to the original Epic images
cover.urlHint: Paste a direct image link and click {button} to test it in the preview box above.
cover.fileLabel: Select a Local File from Computer
cover.fileHint: When you pick a file, the image is processed locally and reflected in the preview above instantly.
cover.sgdbSetupDesc: Thousands of community-made portrait covers (2:3) and spotlight banners for video games.
cover.sgdbWhatTitle: What Is SteamGridDB and Why Is an API Key Required?
cover.sgdbWhatBody: SteamGridDB is a high-quality open image archive for games. To prevent abuse and allow searching directly from your library, a free personal access key (Token) is required.
cover.sgdbStep1: Go to the official SteamGridDB page and sign in (with Steam or Discord).
cover.sgdbStep2: On the page that opens, click "Create API Key" and copy your key.
cover.sgdbStep3: Paste the key into the field below and press "Save and Search".
cover.sgdbGetKey: Get Your Free API Key Here
cover.sgdbLibBody: SteamGridDB is an open platform hosting official and community-made portrait covers (2:3) and spotlight banners (Hero) for video games. The images you pick are applied to your library instantly.
cover.noResults: No suitable image found. Try a different search term.

feat.dualSenseTip: Native DualSense / PlayStation (light bar, audio) and Xbox controllers are supported on PC.
feat.kbMouseTip: The game controls and menus are designed for keyboard and mouse.
feat.xboxGamepadTip: Xbox and XInput-compatible controllers work directly. DualSense may require XInput / DS4Windows.
feat.localSaveTip: Save files are stored on the local disk. You can back them up via the launcher.
feat.onlineServerSaveTip: Your characters and progress sync directly with the game servers and your account.
feat.steamCloudTip: Saves can sync through Steam Cloud. The last write time is shown when Steam recorded it locally.
feat.gogCloudTip: GOG Cloud exists for this game. This launcher cannot see the last sync time without the game's save folder.
feat.partialPadTip: The store lists limited controller support. Keyboard and mouse are the main controls.
feat.ubiCloudTip: Saves sync through Ubisoft Connect's own cloud service.
feat.eaCloudTip: Saves sync through EA's own cloud service.
feat.supportedOfflineTip: Can be played locally without an internet connection.
feat.alwaysOnlineTip: This game is server-based and requires an active internet connection.
feat.partnerRequiredTip: The {name} client and account are required for initial verification/offline mode.
feat.multi4v1Tip: Asymmetric online multiplayer horror with 1 Killer and 4 Survivors.
feat.mmoTip: A persistent online world with a large player community.
feat.singleMultiTip: Includes both a rich single-player story and online multiplayer modes.
feat.singleCoopTip: Playable both solo and co-op with friends.
critic.title: Review & Critic Scores
critic.readOnGoygoy: Read the review on Goygoy Engine
playtime.whyDesc: Playtime is counted while you play (the window may close to the tray; the session keeps running) and merged with Epic's own hours when Epic has them. You can correct the total here; your manual value is never lowered automatically.
playtime.lastActivityHint: Shown in the "Last Activity" field on the library detail card.
playtime.noSession: No session recorded through this launcher yet
controller.noneDesc: Connect a controller over USB or Bluetooth; the launcher detects it automatically.
controller.tvModeDesc: Full-screen 10-ft layout for a TV or a docked Steam Deck. Start / Menu on the pad toggles it.
controller.tvAutoTitle: Open TV Mode when a controller connects
controller.tvAutoDesc: On Steam Deck this defaults to on. On a desktop it stays off unless you enable it here.
controller.deckNote: Steam Deck detected. Built-in controls use the Xbox layout (A play, B back, Y favorite). L2/R2 skip along a row, L4/R4 favorite and details, Menu opens TV Mode.
controller.bridgeDesc: PlayStation controllers are HID devices, so games that only read XInput (for example Dead by Daylight) ignore them. The bridge feeds your controller into a virtual Xbox 360 pad. Turn it off for games that support DualShock natively: they would see two pads.
controller.bridgeNoHid: Could not open the controller HID interface: {a1}
controller.bridgeVirtualNote: The bridge adds a virtual Xbox 360 Controller next to your PlayStation pad; it disappears when the bridge is turned off.
controller.bridgeNoDriver: ViGEmBus is not installed; install the driver to use the bridge.
controller.bridgeError: Could not create the virtual controller: {a1}
controller.bridgeStartTimeout: The bridge did not start in time.
controller.bridgeNotifBody: PlayStation controllers need the XInput bridge for some games. Settings > Controller turns it on.
steam.desc: Reads the games installed by the Steam client on this PC. Games are launched by Steam itself; the launcher never touches their files.
settings.steamExitAfterPlayDesc: Hides the Steam window when a game starts and quits the Steam client after the game closes. Steam stays running during play so DRM still works. Off by default.
settings.clientExitAfterPlayDesc: Quits the client once the game closes. It stays running while you play. Off by default.
steam.empty: The Steam client reports no installed games.
steam.managedByDesc: Files, updates and cloud saves belong to the Steam client; the launcher only opens it.
steam.verifyDesc: Runs Steam's own integrity check on the game files.
steam.playtimeSource: Playtime comes from the Steam client.
steam.uninstallDesc: Removes the game through Steam's own uninstaller.
steam.cloudNoticeDesc: Valve does not share real-time Steam Cloud synchronization status with third-party applications. You can verify sync status directly in the Steam client, or use Efxlve Personal Cloud Save Backup (Google Drive / WebDAV) for independent backups.
steam.dlcDesc: Steam lists these add-ons; names and prices are in the store.
gog.dlcDesc: These extras install with the game. Open the GOG store for names and details.
gog.managedByDesc: Install, verify and uninstall run through this launcher. Cloud saves stay with GOG Galaxy.
gog.cloudHint: GOG Cloud is available. Last sync time is not readable here without the game's save folder.
gog.cloudNoticeDesc: GOG Galaxy cloud synchronization is proprietary to the official GOG client. You can sync via GOG Galaxy, or use Efxlve Personal Cloud Save Backup (Google Drive / WebDAV) for independent backups.
gog.verifyBusy: Finish the current GOG download before verifying files.
steam.qrHint: Scan the code with the Steam mobile app and approve the sign-in; this screen updates itself.

manage.epicDataP1: Sessions started from this launcher are counted locally, and Epic's own playtime service is merged on top when it has hours for the game (not every game reports there). Closing the window while you play keeps the launcher in the tray so the session keeps counting.
manage.epicDataP2: Use "Edit Time" above to correct the total manually; a value you set yourself is never lowered automatically.

settings.gogInstallDirHint: GOG games install here by default. If left empty:

settings.eglDesc: Detects games installed by the official Epic Games Launcher and syncs them into your library.
settings.gogGalaxyDesc: Games installed by the official GOG Galaxy client can be imported with full launcher support.
settings.cometDesc: Runs Comet, the open-source GOG Communication Service, while a GOG game plays so achievements unlock without the Galaxy client.
settings.gogGalaxyNone: No games found in GOG Galaxy
settings.eglNone: No extra games installed via Epic Games Launcher were found, or the EGL folder could not be located.
settings.sgdbDesc: Add high-quality portrait covers (2:3) and wide hero art to your games from the SteamGridDB community platform.
settings.steamApiHint: Only needed for games with no local achievement data.
settings.steamApiDesc: Achievements normally come from the Steam client's own cache — no key needed. A few games keep no local data; for those, a free Steam Web API key lets the launcher fetch the achievement list and your unlocks from Steam. Without a key, those games show none.
settings.netMaxDesc: Targets the highest download speed using all available bandwidth and CPU cores.
settings.netLowDesc: Uses few resources in the background and avoids stutter while gaming or browsing.
settings.netBalancedDesc: Delivers ideal download speed without saturating your connection during play.
settings.offlineDesc: Epic: When you have no connection or want to stay offline, it runs the library from the local cache and launches games offline.
settings.compressionDesc: Automatically compresses new screenshots, saving 70-85% of disk space.
settings.avifInfo: AVIF Technology: Thanks to modern AV1 encoding, 12-15 MB raw PNG screenshots are compressed to ~1.2 MB with no visible difference.
settings.webpInfo: WebP (Balanced): smaller than PNG, widely supported, and a good compromise between size and compatibility.
settings.jpgInfo: JPEG (Universal): the safest choice — opens anywhere, but compression artifacts can show at low quality.
settings.compressionOffDesc: With compression off, screenshots are saved directly as original, uncompressed raw PNG.

appUpdate.deferred: The update can be installed once the active download or game session ends.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.subtitle: Connect your store accounts. The launcher opens without an account; each store works on its own.
accounts.groupClients: Stores that live in their own client
accounts.optionalInfo: Accounts are optional; the launcher opens without one. Passwords are never stored — session keys are sealed with Windows DPAPI for this user only.
accounts.clientInfo: These stores keep their games in their own client. The launcher reads the client's library and hands play back to it.

accounts.note.epic: The library and cloud saves come from your Epic account; the launcher does the installing and updating.
accounts.note.gog: Install and uninstall are handed to GOG Galaxy; playtime comes from Galaxy's local record.
accounts.note.steam: The account section manages the library; the client section manages the games installed on this PC. Screenshots stay in Steam's own gallery.
accounts.note.ea: The launcher only launches; downloads and removals happen in the EA app.
accounts.note.ubisoft: Achievements come from the local Ubisoft Connect cache, so a game must be opened once in the client.
accounts.note.xbox: The library comes from your title history and installed Store packages; installation happens in the Microsoft Store.
accounts.note.battlenet: There is no achievement or official playtime feed; playtime counts only sessions started from the launcher.
accounts.note.riot: All four titles are free to play; the library appears as soon as the Riot client is installed.

cloud.guideBtnTip: Step-by-step guide to get a free Google Cloud Client ID
cloud.guideSub: Create and connect your personal Google Cloud project for free in 2 minutes.
cloud.guideStep1: 1. Create a Project in Google Cloud Console
cloud.guideStep1Desc: Go to Google Cloud Console and create a 'New Project' from the top bar (e.g. 'Efxlve Cloud').
cloud.guideStep2Desc: In the left sidebar, navigate to 'APIs & Services > OAuth Consent Screen'. Select 'External' user type and click 'Create'.
cloud.guideStep3Desc: Enter app name ('Efxlve Launcher') and your email. In Scopes, click 'Add or Remove Scopes' and select 'drive.appdata'.
cloud.guideStep4: 4. Add Yourself as a Test User
cloud.guideStep4Desc: Under 'Test Users', click 'Add Users' and enter your Gmail address. This allows you to use your app indefinitely without public Google verification.
cloud.guideStep5Desc: Go to 'Credentials > Create Credentials > OAuth Client ID'. Select application type as 'Desktop App'.
cloud.guideStep6: 6. Paste Your Client ID in Efxlve
cloud.guideStep6Desc: Copy the generated 'Client ID' and 'Client Secret', paste them into Efxlve Launcher settings, and click 'Save'.
cloud.guideStep7Desc: Click 'Connect with Google' in the Launcher. In the opened browser window, choose your test account and click 'Continue / Allow' to finish.
